jd.title: Payroll Account Manager
jd.summary: Procare HR is hiring a Payroll Account Manager to own end-to-end payroll delivery for a multi-client book of business. This is a client-facing seat — you'll be the go-to person clients trust for accurate, on-time, compliant payroll across multiple entities.
jd.summary2: You'll process payroll for multiple clients with multiple EINs, resolve payroll issues with sound judgment, and build the kind of relationships that make clients stick around. Fully remote. $26–$30/hr, credit given for experience.
mustHave: 3+ years processing payroll for multiple clients (multi-state a plus).
2+ years with HRIS platforms (UKG Ready preferred).
Strong Microsoft Office skills, especially Excel.
niceToHave: Associate's degree in Accounting, Business, HR, or Finance.
Prior PEO / HR Shared Services experience.
Comfortable owning client relationships, not just processing.

lookFor.detail: Has actually run payroll across 8+ EINs, not just "supported a team that did." This is the rarest, most important filter.
Understands the operating model of serving many unrelated clients at once — different pay cycles, different rules, same week.
Title says "Account Manager" — they need to own the relationship, not just push numbers through a system quietly.
UKG Ready experience is a green flag, but any modern HRIS (ADP WFN, Paycom, Paylocity, iSolved) with real depth transfers fast.

questions.q: Walk me through how many clients and EINs you've processed payroll for at once — what did that workflow actually look like?
questions.internal: This is the hardest filter to fill. Vague answers ("I helped with a few clients") usually mean single-EIN, in-house experience dressed up. Push for specifics — how many EINs, how they tracked deadlines across them.

questions.q: Have you worked in a PEO or HR shared-services model? What was different about that versus in-house payroll?
questions.internal: PEO experience is "nice to have" on paper but it's actually a strong predictor of success here — the operating model is genuinely different from in-house payroll. Listen for real understanding, not just a resume line.

questions.q: Tell me about a time a client had a payroll issue or dispute. How did you handle it?
questions.internal: This role is titled "Account Manager" for a reason — the client wants someone who owns the relationship under pressure, not just someone who's technically correct and disappears when it gets uncomfortable.

questions.q: What HRIS platforms have you used, and how deep is your experience with UKG Ready specifically?
questions.internal: UKG Ready is preferred, not required — don't screen out a strong candidate on ADP/Paycom/Paylocity/iSolved experience. Listen for depth on any platform (built reports, ran multi-client processing) versus surface-level exposure.

matrices.boolean: ("Payroll Account Manager" OR "Payroll Specialist" OR "Payroll Coordinator" OR "Payroll Analyst") AND ("multi-client" OR "multi-state" OR PEO OR "shared services" OR "multiple EINs") AND ("UKG" OR "UKG Ready" OR "UltiPro" OR "ADP Workforce Now" OR Paycom OR Paylocity OR iSolved)

watchOuts.note: Strong in-house payroll admin with zero multi-client exposure will struggle with the volume and context-switching this role demands.
Technically sharp but avoids client conversations — wrong shape for a role titled "Account Manager."
Associate's degree is preferred, not required — don't auto-reject strong experience-only candidates.

jd.title: Leave of Absence Specialist
jd.summary: Procare HR is hiring a Leave of Absence Specialist to administer leave and accommodations across a multi-client PEO book — FMLA, ADA, state and local leave law, and short- and long-term disability. This seat owns each case from the employee's first notice through return to work.
jd.summary2: Sits in HR Admin and Compliance, reporting to the Leave & Disability Accommodations Manager. Fully remote, Monday–Friday 8AM–5PM in the employee's own time zone. Beyond casework you'll advise managers where leave law collides with PTO, workers' comp and disability benefits, run weekly LOA status reporting, audit leave data for compliance, and mentor other LOA staff. $30/hr, contract.
mustHave: 3+ years administering leave of absence and FMLA in a multi-state organization.
Working knowledge of FMLA, ADA, workers' compensation, STD, LTD and state paid-leave programs.
Has owned the full FMLA lifecycle — eligibility, designation, certification, intermittent tracking, return to work.
HRIS and leave-management system experience, tracking cases including pay and attendance.
Strong Excel — the seat carries weekly LOA reporting and recurring compliance audits.
niceToHave: PEO or HR shared-services experience (the PD calls this highly desirable).
ADA interactive process and reasonable-accommodation casework.
General OSHA regulation and benefit-plan knowledge.
Has mentored or advised other LOA team members.

lookFor.detail: Running FMLA alongside state paid-leave programs — CA CFRA/PFL, NY PFL, WA PFML, CO FAMLI — across multiple client companies. This is the rarest, most important filter. Ask which states, not how many.
Serving many unrelated employers at once is a different job from one in-house population: different policies, different accruals, different managers to chase, same week.
Look for eligibility determinations and designation notices they issued themselves. "I handled FMLA" often means they filed paperwork someone else adjudicated.
This person calls employees during the worst week of their year, and still has to hold a line. Warmth without the ability to say no is a risk, not a strength.

questions.q: Walk me through one FMLA case you owned from the employee's initial notice through return to work. What was your role at each step?
questions.internal: Listen for the unglamorous middle — the certification request, the designation notice, the recertification clock. People who only supported a leave team skip from "they called out" straight to "they came back."

questions.q: Which state paid-leave programs have you administered alongside federal FMLA, and across how many states and client companies at once?
questions.internal: The hardest filter in the search. A case count with no states behind it is a soft answer — push once: "which states?" If the follow-up stays vague, this is single-employer experience dressed up.

questions.q: Tell me about a medical certification that came back incomplete, or an employee whose protected leave ran out. How did you handle it with them and with their manager?
questions.internal: Where the role gets hard and where Procare carries risk. Good answers show process — written notice, a cure period, a documented decision. Weak answers show improvisation, or handing it straight to legal.

questions.q: What leave-management and HRIS systems have you used, and how deep does that go — intake, tracking, reporting, or all three?
questions.internal: Any modern HRIS transfers. What does not transfer is having only ever read a dashboard someone else built. Push for what they configured or reported out of it.

matrices.boolean: ("Leave of Absence Specialist" OR "LOA Specialist" OR "Leave Administrator" OR "Absence Management" OR "Disability and Leave" OR "FMLA Coordinator") AND (FMLA AND (ADA OR "short-term disability" OR STD OR LTD OR "workers compensation")) AND ("multi-state" OR multistate OR PEO OR "shared services" OR "multiple clients" OR CFRA OR PFML OR FAMLI)

watchOuts.note: Every HR Generalist lists FMLA because they sat near it. Filter for who carried the case load, not who supported someone who did.
Open enrollment and carrier feeds are a different muscle from adjudicating eligibility and issuing designation notices.
If a third party made the eligibility call, the candidate coordinated leave — they did not administer it.
